taxonomyNote: NatureServe treats Hypsiglena chlorophaea and H. ochrorhyncha as separate species following Mulcahy (2008), who split the former H. torquata; Colorado Parks and Wildlife lists the Colorado animals as H. jani and H. chlorophaea, and Idaho Fish and Game lists several H. torquata names under chlorophaea.
behavior: Eats mainly lizards and lizard eggs (NatureServe).
Spends inactive periods under rocks or other surface cover, in crevices or underground (NatureServe).
habitat: Arid and semiarid plains, canyons and hillsides, usually rocky, dissected terrain with sandy or gravelly soil, including desert, grassland, shrubland, savanna and woodland (NatureServe).
range: Northern California south through western California to southern Baja California (NatureServe).
